title: Baked Salmon en Croute
subtitle: Salmon fillet wrapped in rough puff pastry with spinach and dill
excerpt: Salmon en croute wraps a whole salmon fillet in flaky rough puff pastry with a layer of wilted spinach, dill, and creme fraiche. It looks impressive but the method is straightforward. The pastry seals in moisture so the salmon stays tender.
sourceNotes: En croute (in a crust) is a French technique applied widely to fish and meat. Salmon en croute became a British dinner-party staple from the 1970s and remains popular for celebrations and Sunday meals.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 4 hours ahead and keep covered in the fridge. Brush with egg wash just before baking.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 180C / Gas 6. The oven must be fully preheated before the parcel goes in.

content.text: Squeeze every drop of water from the wilted spinach before you spread it on the pastry. Any moisture left in will make the pastry soggy from the inside.

items.prepNote: one whole piece, skin off, pin-boned

content.text: Make the pastry: mix the flour and a pinch of salt. Add the cold butter cubes. Use your fingertips to press the butter into flat sheets through the flour. Do not rub it in fully. Add 6 to 7 tablespoons of ice-cold water and bring together into a rough dough. Chill for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mix the spinach, dill, creme fraiche, and lemon zest together. Season well.
Roll the pastry on a lightly floured surface into a rectangle large enough to wrap the salmon fully, about 35cm x 30cm.
Spread half the spinach mixture down the centre of the pastry. Lay the salmon on top. Spread the rest of the spinach over the salmon.
Fold the pastry over the salmon and press the edges firmly to seal. Crimp with a fork. Transfer to the baking tray, seam side down.
Brush all over with egg wash. Score the top lightly with a knife. Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until golden.
Rest for 5 minutes before slicing. Serve with a green salad and extra lemon.

items.cause: Spinach was too wet or baking tray was cold.
items.fix: Preheat the tray; squeeze spinach very dry next time.

items.cause: Edges were not sealed firmly enough.
items.fix: Press edges hard and crimp with a fork before baking.
